content.content:
1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison and replay decision) queries, the reservation/alert
85	  listings (including the region alert listing),
86	  `GET /events/region/replay/decisions`,
87	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
88	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/events/replay/decisions`,
89	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources`,
90	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations`,
91	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events`,
92	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region`,
93	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/aggregate`,
94	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region/aggregate`,
95	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/replay/decisions`,
96	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region/replay/decisions`,
97	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
98	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/replay/decisions`,
99	  `POST /branches/compare/events`,
100	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
101	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
102	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
103	  `POST /snapshots/compare/replay/decisions`,
104	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
105	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`,
106	  `POST /snapshots/{snapshotId}/decisions/evaluate`, and the other
107	  read-only branch entry points.
108	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
109	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
110	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
111	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
112	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
113	
114	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
115	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
116	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
117	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
118	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
119	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
120	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
121	is `403`, never `404`.
122	
123	## Event ledger
124	
125	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
126	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
127	
128	### `POST /events`
129	
130	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
131	exactly these five top-level fields:
132	
133	| Field          | Rule                                      |
134	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
135	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
136	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
137	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
138	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
139	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
140	
141	```bash
142	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
143	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
144	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
145	```
146	
147	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
148	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
149	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
150	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
151	  the other fields differ.
152	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
153	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
154	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
155	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
156	
157	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
158	
159	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
160	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
161	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
162	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
163	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
164	
165	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
166	
167	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
168	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
169	organizations' data is never included.
170	
171	Query parameters:
172	
173	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
174	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
175	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
176	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
177	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
178	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
179	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
180	
181	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
182	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
183	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
184	
185	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
186	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
187	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
188	
189	```json
190	{
191	  "organizationId": "org-1",
192	  "type": "incident.created",
193	  "windowSize": 60,
194	  "from": null,
195	  "to": null,
196	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
197	}
198	```
199	
200	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
201	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
202	  `windows` is `[]`.
203	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
204	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
205	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
206	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
207	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
208	
209	```bash
210	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
211	```
212	
213	### Region attribution
214	
215	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
216	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
217	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
218	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
219	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
220	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
221	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
222	
223	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
224	
225	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
226	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
227	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
228	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
229	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
230	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
231	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
232	point and a trailing newline.
233	
234	```bash
235	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
236	```
237	
238	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
239	
240	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
241	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
242	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
243	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
244	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
245	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
246	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
247	newline):
248	
249	```json
250	{
251	  "organizationId": "org-1",
252	  "region": "north",
253	  "type": "incident.created",
254	  "windowSize": 60,
255	  "from": null,
256	  "to": null,
257	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
258	}
259	```
260	
261	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
262	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
263	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
264	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
265	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
266	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
267	
268	```bash
269	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
270	```
271	
272	### `GET /events/replay/decisions?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...&threshold=...`
273	
274	A read-only, step-by-step recomputation of the window counts and peak
275	decision as matching events enter a replay one at a time. The ledger,
276	reservation inventory, and alerts are never written; identical requests
277	return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials
278	may call it. The query parameters are:
279	
280	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
281	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
282	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
283	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
284	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
285	| `threshold`      | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `3`)              |
286	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
287	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
288	
289	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
290	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, blank, or invalid parameter
291	yields `422` with `validation_error`.

294	organizations' data never enters the result. The matching events are
295	ordered by `occurredAt` ascending and then `eventId` in Unicode code-point
296	order, and accumulated into the replay in that order. Each replay step
297	reports the event's `eventId` and `occurredAt`, the window-count rows for
298	every event accumulated up to and including that one, and the peak decision
299	at that point. Windows start at `0` and each covers
300	`[start, start + windowSize)`:

303	  events appear.
304	- With `from`/`to`, events outside the closed interval `[from, to]` still
305	  arrive as replay steps in order, but every window intersecting the
306	  interval is returned at every step, including empty windows with
307	  `count: 0`, exactly like the ranged aggregate.
308	- The peak is the largest window count; ties resolve to the earliest
309	  start. `action` is `"escalate"` when the peak reaches `threshold` and
310	  `"observe"` otherwise. With no matching events there are no steps at
311	  all; a step whose accumulated prefix has no counted window carries
312	  `peakCount: 0`, `peakStart: null`, and `"observe"`.

318	range, and carries the ordered `steps` array. It is compact JSON with

320	trailing newline:

322	```json

324	```

419	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
420	
421	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
422	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
423	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
424	object containing exactly these fields:
425	
426	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
427	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
428	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
429	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
430	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
431	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
432	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
433	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
434	
435	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
436	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
437	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
438	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
439	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
440	ones for audit reconciliation.
441	
442	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
443	
444	```json
445	{
446	  "organizationId": "org-1",
447	  "type": "incident.created",
448	  "windowSize": 60,
449	  "from": null,
450	  "to": null,
451	  "peakStart": 60,
452	  "peakCount": 2,
453	  "action": "observe"
454	}
455	```
456	
457	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
458	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
459	  regardless of event submission order.
460	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
461	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
462	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
463	  `"observe"`.
464	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
465	  other organizations' data is never included.

467	```bash
468	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
469	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
470	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
471	```

475	  produced.

479	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
480	
481	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
482	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
483	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
484	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
485	exactly these fields:
486	
487	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
488	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
489	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
490	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
491	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
492	
493	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
494	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
495	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
496	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
497	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
498	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
499	
500	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
501	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
502	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
503	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
504	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
505	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
506	demands.
507	
508	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
509	
510	```json
511	{
512	  "organizationId": "org-1",
513	  "assignments": [
514	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
515	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
516	  ],
517	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
518	  "totalUnits": 6
519	}
520	```
521	
522	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
523	  processing order.
524	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
525	  `demandId`.
526	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
527	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
528	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
529	
530	```bash
531	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
532	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
533	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
534	```
535	
536	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
537	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
538	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
539	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.

541	## Reservation inventory
542	
543	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
544	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
545	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
546	is never rewritten afterwards.
547	
548	### `POST /reservations`
549	
550	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
551	with exactly these five top-level fields:
552	
553	| Field           | Rule                                      |
554	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
555	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
556	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
557	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
558	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
559	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
560	
561	```bash
562	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
563	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
564	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
565	```
566	
567	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
568	and a trailing newline:
569	
570	```json
571	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
572	```
573	
574	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
575	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
576	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
577	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
578	
579	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
580	  resource also establishes its capacity.
581	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
582	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
583	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
584	  exists but the other fields differ.
585	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
586	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
587	  capacity is never rewritten.
588	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
589	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
590	  unchanged.
591	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
592	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
593	  is produced.
594	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
595	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
596	
597	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
598	
599	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
600	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
601	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
602	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
603	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
604	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
605	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
606	`422`.

608	## Alert suppression and escalation
609	
610	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
611	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
612	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
613	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
614	paths are added.
615	
616	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
617	
618	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
619	containing exactly these fields:
620	
621	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
622	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
623	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
624	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
625	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
626	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
627	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
628	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
629	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
630	
631	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
632	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
633	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
634	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
635	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
636	
637	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
638	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
639	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
640	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
641	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
642	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
643	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
644	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
645	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
646	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
647	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
648	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
649	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
650	    organization/type always creates an alert.
651	
652	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
653	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
654	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
655	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
656	trailing newline):
657	
658	```json
659	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
660	```
661	
662	```bash
663	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
664	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
665	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
666	```
667	
668	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
669	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
670	  written.
671	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
672	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
673	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
674	
675	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
676	
677	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
678	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
679	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
680	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
681	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
682	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
683	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
684	
685	### `POST /alerts/region/evaluate`
686	
687	The region-dimension counterpart of `POST /alerts/evaluate`, scoped to one
688	region. Requires a `write` credential and
689	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
690	exactly these fields:
691	
692	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
693	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
694	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
695	| `region`            | required, non-empty string, matched verbatim                 |
696	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
697	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
698	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
699	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
700	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
701	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
702	
703	Only the organization's events whose payload `region` is a non-empty string
704	equal to the requested region (matched verbatim, no normalization) and whose
705	`type` matches are counted; events without a region never match, an unknown
706	region simply computes as zero events and is never implicitly created, and
707	other organizations' data is never included. The peak uses the exact same
708	windowing as `POST /alerts/evaluate`: windows start at `0` and cover
709	`[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the earliest window start,
710	and the event ledger is never modified.
711	
712	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
713	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
714	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
715	  most recent prior region alert for the same organization, region, and
716	  type:
717	  - `peakStart - priorStart >= suppressionWindow` creates a new alert;
718	    `action` is `"escalate"`, `alertId` is the new id, and
719	    `suppressedCount` is `0`.
720	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
721	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
722	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
723	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
724	    organization/region/type always creates an alert.
725	
726	Region-dimension alerts share the one global identifier sequence with
727	organization-dimension alerts (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, … across all
728	organizations, regions, and types), but the two kinds never suppress each
729	other: each kind compares only against its own most recent alert. The
730	suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under one
731	lock — the same lock that makes the organization/role decision — so
732	concurrent threshold hits open exactly one alert and a rejected request
733	leaves no trace. The `200` response echoes every request parameter and adds
734	the result fields (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, integer values,
735	one trailing newline):
736	
737	```json

739	```
740	
741	```bash
742	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/region/evaluate \
743	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
744	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
745	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","region":"north","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
746	```

748	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
749	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
750	  content.
751	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is read-only
752	  or its organization differs from the body's; the credential and
753	  organization are judged before any business computation, and no alert is
754	  written.
755	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
756	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
757	  written.
758	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body,

789	## Snapshots and branches
790	
791	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
792	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
793	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
794	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
795	the main service or with other branches.
796	
797	### Organization boundaries
798	
799	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
800	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
801	scoped to that boundary:
802	
803	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
804	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
805	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
806	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
807	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
808	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
809	  organization's data never changes them.
810	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
811	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
812	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
813	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
814	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
815	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
816	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
817	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
818	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
819	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
820	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
821	  namespaced per organization.
822	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
823	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
824	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
825	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
826	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
827	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
828	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
829	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
830	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
831	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
832	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
833	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
834	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
835	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
836	
837	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
838	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
839	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
840	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
841	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.
842	
843	### `POST /snapshots`
844	
845	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
846	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
847	
848	| Field        | Rule                     |
849	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
850	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |

852	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
853	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
854	JSON and one trailing newline, matching the byte contract of the other write
855	entry points:

857	```json
858	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
859	```

861	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
862	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
863	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
864	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
865	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
866	  content is never replaced or mutated.
867	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
868	  organization; no snapshot is stored.

872	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.

884	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources?organizationId=...`

890	or in the main service is read for mutation or written: the main-service
891	event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert state are untouched, failed

1246	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
1247	}
1248	```
1249	
1250	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
1251	  actually covered by matching captured events are returned; with no
1252	  matching events `windows` is `[]`.
1253	- With `from`/`to`, only captured events with `from <= occurredAt <= to`
1254	  count, and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is
1255	  returned, including empty windows with `count: 0`.
1256	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
1257	  regardless of event insertion order.
1258	
1259	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer values
1260	kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1261	
1262	```json
1263	{"from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","region":"north","snapshotId":"snap-1","to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"count":2,"end":60,"start":0}]}
1264	```
1265	
1266	```bash
1267	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180' \
1268	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
1269	```
1270	
1271	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the query
1272	shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
1273	
1274	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
1275	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
1276	  content.
1277	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a parameter is missing,
1278	  duplicated, blank, or invalid: a non-positive-integer `windowSize`,
1279	  unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
1280	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
1281	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot belongs
1282	  to another organization.
1283	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
1284	  has never existed; an aggregate never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1285	
1286	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
1287	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1288	
1289	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/replay/decisions?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...&threshold=...`
1290	
1291	A read-only, step-by-step recomputation of the window counts and peak
1292	decision over one snapshot's captured events for the caller's organization —
1293	the single-snapshot counterpart of `GET /events/replay/decisions`, lowering
1294	the exact window and peak contract of the main replay-decision query onto
1295	the events the snapshot captured at its creation time. Snapshots are
1296	immutable, so nothing in the snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service
1297	is read for mutation or written: the main-service event ledger, reservation
1298	inventory, and alert state are untouched, failed requests leave no trace,
1299	and identical requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and
1300	`write` credentials may call it.
1301	
1302	Query parameters follow the exact same rules as
1303	`GET /events/replay/decisions`:
1304	
1305	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
1306	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
